canonical_edition: Fragmenta, FHG 2: 344. Q: 249: Hist. frr. 1–2 (fr. 2 verba Latina solum)
sources_tested: Exact Canon FHG II p.344; item-level FHG/DFHG witness and attribution check; local First1KGreek Zenobius TEI 4.38 plus its licence header; Bibliotheca Palatina item metadata; Servius ad Aen. 6.14 verified at Packhum/Monumenta; data/scan_sources.csv exact FHG II record
open_text_result: Fr. 1 is fully available in the CC-BY-SA First1KGreek Zenobius 4.38 TEI: the Ino narrative names ‘Menekrates the Tyrian’ but the FHG apparatus also records the doubt ‘the Lycian?’. Fr. 2 survives only in Latin, exactly as the Canon warns: Servius ad Aen. 6.14 says that Menecrates related Daedalus’ flight to Crete and Icarus’ shipwreck; it concludes that the commentator does not know which Menecrates is meant. The checked online Servius texts have no verified reuse licence.
open_text_license: Fr. 1: CC BY-SA 4.0 explicitly in the First1KGreek TEI publication statement. Fr. 2: Latin Packhum/Monumenta access checked, but no project-compatible text-reuse licence verified.
scan_result: The exact FHG II scan is registered as Internet Archive fragmentahistori02unse and sampled visually good; reuse permission for its images is not explicit, so it is not queued.
scan_rights: Public-domain-era edition; no explicit Internet Archive image-reuse licence recorded. No image or provider OCR used.
next_action: Retain the licensed Zenobius text as FHG fr.1 with provenance. Keep Servius fr.2 as a citation-only lead until an explicitly licensed transcription is found. Do not normalize either fragment under a securely Tyrian author without resolving the Lycius/anonymous doubts; clarify image rights before any scan workflow.
notes: The Palatina catalogue independently identifies Zenobius 4.38 as Menecrates Tyrius fr.6 Müller. Servius’ own closing note (‘Haec cuiusnam Menecratis sint nescio’) makes the assignment of FHG fr.7 especially insecure. DFHG was used only for bibliographic/witness verification, not as a source text: its site documents an OCR-derived digital edition.
